front.title: Relational Echo Calculus (REC): A Transformation-First Mathematical Communication Prototype

abstract.t: This document describes a transformation-first teaching notation for mathematical communication to unfamiliar receivers. The prototype operates on finite motifs drawn from the vertices of a Hamming hypercube. Echo operations act through coordinate permutations and binary translations. We distinguish invariance of a coarse signature from proof of exact orbit equivalence, exhibiting two four- dimensional patterns that have equal pairwise-distance multisets but different induced adjacency. A synthetic toy decoder reconstructs arbitrary token meanings when its complete transformation hypothesis class is supplied. The main testable conjecture is that instruction ordered by invariance might improve cross-agent decoding over instruction ordered by arithmetic under matched information budgets. The conjecture has not been experimentally evaluated; no new extraterrestrial signal or new mathematical theorem is claimed.
